meta.title: Golem Docs: edit Word, PDF, Markdown, and more in your browser
meta.description: Golem Docs is a document editor that lives in your browser. Open, edit and convert Word, OpenDocument, PDF, Markdown, HTML, and plain text, free and with no account. A subscription adds sync across devices, sharing and live editing together, and an AI assistant.
meta.ogDescription: One editor for every kind of document. Open, edit and convert Word, PDF, Markdown, and more, free in your browser with no account. Subscribe to sync, share and edit together, and use the AI assistant.
hero.title: I wanted one editor for everything.
hero.lede: Drop in a Word file, a PDF, a Markdown note, a CSV, an SVG, or just about any other document and start editing, in an editor that feels like Word 2003. I built it because I wanted it.
hero.fine: Free in your browser, with no account and no ads. Sync, sharing, and AI are $5 a month.
story.title: Why I built this
story.p1: I'm David. Obsidian runs my life, but PDFs kept getting in the way: I was always hunting for a tool to convert one or edit one. ZIP files made it more interesting, because an archive can hold anything, so an editor that opens one has to open whatever is inside. I thought it would be fun if it could open every kind of document there is, and I have been building toward that ever since.
story.p2: Much of the code was written with Claude, with me steering (I promise I could have coded it myself, but it would have taken years). Golem Docs is still growing, so if a file won't open the way it should, tell me and it goes on the list.
sheet.title: Grandma's lasagna
sheet.p1: Typed up in Word, kept as Markdown in my notes, printed as a PDF for the fridge. It is the same recipe the whole way
sheet.p2: Golem Docs draws the page itself, so it looks the way it will print.
features.title: Built to open whatever I throw at it.
features.sub: Most editors handle one format well. I wanted one that handles them all.
f.convert.p: Switch between Word, Markdown, and web pages. Switch back and your formatting returns.
f.pdf.h: Edit PDFs, not just mark them up
f.pdf.p: Edit text in place, redact, rearrange pages, fill in forms, and annotate.
f.pdf.link: Everything you can do with a PDF →
f.images.p: Crop, resize, and annotate PNG, JPEG, and WebP images, or pixelate what to hide.
f.layout.p: Word-style layout with tables, columns, comments, and LaTeX math. It prints as it looks.
f.live.p: Share a link and edit the same document together, with live changes and cursors. Sharing needs my server, so it is part of the subscription; editing on your own is free.
f.ai.p: The AI assistant reads your document, rewrites or adds paragraphs, changes styles, and leaves comments. Undo takes any change back. It is part of the subscription because every request costs me money.
f.save.p: No Save button. Changes are kept as you make them, even offline.
f.word.p: Word 2003 menus, toolbars, and dialogs. No ribbon to hunt through.
f.you.p: Choose a color scheme with dark mode, arrange toolbars, and use 11 languages.
f.large.p: Open a 50 MB log and scroll, search, and filter without freezing.
f.import.p: Import a file, a whole folder, or a ZIP, and keep its folders. Moving from Obsidian? Import your vault.
f.search.p: Find words and #tags across all your documents, with results that open at the matching paragraph. It works offline from your browser's own index.
f.obsidian.p: Your vault is a folder of Markdown notes. Import it and your notes arrive in their folders.
perf.title: Fast, even on War and Peace.
perf.sub: Here is all 1,006 pages of it in Page Grid, zooming from the whole book down to a single paragraph and back. The editor draws every page itself on your graphics card, so big documents stay responsive.
perf.alt: A screen recording of War and Peace, all 1,006 pages, zooming from the Page Grid view in to readable text and back out.
formats.title: If you can name it, you can probably open it.
formats.sub: Drop a file onto the window, or choose Open. Convert it to another format, or download a file for someone else. Older .doc files save as .docx, and GIF, BMP, and SVG pictures as PNG. See what each conversion keeps.
steps.title: Up and running in a minute.
steps.sub: There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for.
s1.p: Drop a file onto the window, or start a new blank one.
s2.p: Type, format, mark up a PDF, or switch to Markdown with Convert To.
s3.p: Download a file for someone else, no account needed. Or subscribe and send a link to edit together.
pricing.title: Free to use. Paying covers my server and AI bills.
pricing.sub: Editing runs in your browser, so it costs me nothing to give away, and Golem Docs works fully without an account. Sync and sharing need a server and storage, and the AI assistant costs money every time it answers. The subscription is $5 a month: it pays for those, and what is left over lets me keep working on Golem Docs. Cancel any time.
p1.p: Edit, convert, and download as much as you like. Documents are saved in your browser and never sent to me.
p2.p: Sync keeps your documents on my server so they follow you to any device. Sharing lets people edit together, live. The AI assistant is billed to me for each request. Sign in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub, or Apple to subscribe.
p3.h: Opening what others share is free
p3.p: If a subscriber shares a document with you, you only need to sign in to open it, and to edit it if they let you.
p4.p: Your documents stay in your browser, and downloading a file, or all your files zipped, never needs an account or a subscription.
privacy.title: Your documents are yours.
privacy.sub: I wrote the privacy policy to be read. It is short, and it says what I collect and why.
v1.p: I don't sell your data and I don't show ads.
v2.p: No analytics and no advertising trackers.
v3.p: Every document is a real file that belongs to you. File ▸ Download All saves everything you have kept as one ZIP, any time, no account needed.
closing.title: Open a document and see.
closing.sub: It runs in your browser, so the fastest way to judge it is to use it. If something is broken or missing, email me.
